content: What is the application deadline for first-year students?

For first-year students at Texas State University, the application deadlines are: Fall semester - March 1st (priority), May 1st (regular); Spring semester - December 1st; Summer semester - May 1st. Early Action deadline is October 15th. To ensure scholarship consideration, apply by the priority deadline. Submit both your application and all required documents by these dates.
Are SAT or ACT scores required for undergraduate admission?

Texas State University is currently test-optional through 2024. While SAT/ACT scores are not required for admission, submitting them may qualify you for additional scholarship opportunities and can strengthen your application. If you choose not to submit test scores, your admission will be based on your high school rank, GPA, and academic course rigor.
How can I apply for early decision, and when is the deadline?

Texas State University offers Early Action (non-binding) rather than Early Decision. The Early Action deadline is October 15th. By applying Early Action, you'll receive an admission decision by late November/early December. This option allows you to apply early while still keeping your options open, as it's not binding like Early Decision programs at other universities.
Is there an application fee, and how much is it?

Yes, there is a non-refundable application fee of $75 for domestic students and $90 for international students when applying to Texas State University. This fee must be paid when submitting your application through ApplyTexas. If you need assistance with the fee, you may be eligible for an application fee waiver.
Can I get a fee waiver for the application fee?

Yes, fee waivers are available for eligible students who demonstrate financial need. You may qualify if you: receive a SAT/ACT fee waiver, participate in the Free/Reduced Lunch program, are a Pell Grant recipient, or participate in other qualifying federal/state assistance programs. Submit your fee waiver request through your high school counselor or through the admissions office before applying.
What documents do I need to submit with my application?

For a complete application to Texas State, you need to submit: 1) Completed ApplyTexas application, 2) Official high school transcript showing class rank and GPA, 3) SAT/ACT scores (optional through 2024), 4) Application fee or fee waiver, 5) Official college transcripts if you have dual credit. International students must also submit TOEFL/IELTS scores and foreign credential evaluation.
How do I know if my high school courses meet admission requirements?

Texas State requires completion of the Texas Foundation High School Program or equivalent. Required courses include: 4 years of English, 3-4 years of Mathematics (including Algebra I, Geometry, and Algebra II), 3-4 years of Science (including Biology and Chemistry/Physics), 3-4 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of the same Foreign Language. Your high school counselor can help verify if your courses meet these requirements.
What are the minimum GPA requirements for undergraduate admission?

Texas State uses a sliding scale that combines class rank/GPA with standardized test scores. Generally, students in the top 10% of their class are automatically admitted. For others, the minimum GPA requirement varies: students with a 3.3+ GPA may be admitted without test scores, while those with lower GPAs need to meet specific SAT/ACT score requirements. The university recommends a minimum 2.5 GPA for consideration.
Can international students apply as undergraduates?

Yes, international students can apply as undergraduates to Texas State University. Requirements include: completed ApplyTexas application, official secondary school transcripts with English translation, proof of English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS scores), financial documentation showing ability to pay for studies, copy of passport, and a $90 application fee. Additional requirements may apply based on your country of origin.
What English proficiency tests are accepted for international applicants?

Texas State accepts several English proficiency tests: TOEFL (minimum 78 iBT/550 PBT), IELTS (minimum 6.5), Duolingo English Test (minimum 110), PTE Academic (minimum 52), or Cambridge C1 Advanced (minimum 176). Exemptions are available for students from English-speaking countries or those who completed high school in the U.S. Some academic programs may require higher scores.
Does Texas State University offer conditional admission?

Yes, Texas State offers conditional admission through the PACE (Personalized Academic and Career Exploration) program for students who don't meet regular admission requirements. Conditionally admitted students must maintain specific GPA requirements, meet regularly with academic advisors, and complete certain first-year requirements. International students may receive conditional admission pending completion of English language requirements.
How long does it take to receive an admissions decision?

Texas State typically provides admissions decisions within 2-4 weeks after receiving all required application materials. Early Action applicants receive decisions by late November/early December. Regular admission decisions are rolling, meaning they're sent out as applications are reviewed. You can check your application status online through your applicant portal. Processing times may be longer during peak application periods.
Can I apply if I have a GED instead of a high school diploma?

Yes, Texas State accepts applications from students with a GED (General Educational Development) certificate. GED holders must submit their official GED test scores and may need to meet additional requirements, such as minimum test scores or completion of college preparatory courses. SAT/ACT scores are recommended but not required through 2024. Contact the admissions office for specific requirements based on your situation.
Are transfer students required to submit high school transcripts?

Transfer students with 30 or more transferable college credit hours are not required to submit high school transcripts. However, if you have fewer than 30 transferable hours, you must submit both high school and college transcripts. All transfer students must submit official transcripts from every college or university previously attended, regardless of whether credits were earned.
What GPA do transfer students need for admission?

Transfer students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in all transferable college coursework. Some competitive programs may require higher GPAs for admission. Students with fewer than 30 transferable hours must also meet freshman admission requirements. All grades from previous college coursework, including repeated courses, are calculated in the transfer GPA.
Are there specific requirements for students applying to the honors program?

Yes, the Honors College has additional requirements. First-year applicants typically need: minimum 3.5 high school GPA, competitive SAT/ACT scores if submitted, and a completed Honors College application with essay. Current and transfer students need a minimum 3.5 college GPA. All applicants must submit a separate Honors College application after being admitted to Texas State. The program looks for students who demonstrate intellectual curiosity and community engagement.
Can I apply to Texas State University with a dual-credit high school transcript?

Yes, you can apply with dual-credit coursework. Submit both your high school transcript and official college transcripts for all dual-credit courses. Dual credits from accredited institutions may count toward your degree if you earn a grade of C or better. These credits may also affect your classification and registration priority, but admission decisions for first-year students are still primarily based on your high school record.
Is an interview required for the admission process?

No, Texas State University does not require interviews as part of the general admission process. However, some specific programs or scholarships may require interviews after admission. International students may be asked to complete an online video interview to demonstrate English proficiency. The admissions office welcomes meetings with prospective students, but these are optional and informational only.
How do I submit my transcripts and test scores?

Official transcripts must be sent directly from your school either electronically through approved services (TREx, Parchment, National Student Clearinghouse) or by mail in a sealed envelope. SAT scores should be sent using code 6667, and ACT scores using code 4178. International transcripts must be evaluated by a recognized credential evaluation service. Electronic submissions are preferred and typically process faster than mailed documents.
Can I submit my application before taking the SAT/ACT?

Yes, you can submit your application before taking or submitting SAT/ACT scores. Texas State is test-optional through 2024, so scores are not required for admission. If you plan to submit scores later, you can update your application by having official scores sent directly from the testing agency. Remember that while scores aren't required for admission, they may be needed for certain scholarships or programs.
Are homeschooled students eligible for admission?

Yes, homeschooled students are eligible for admission to Texas State. You must submit a home school transcript with courses, grades, and completion date. The transcript should be signed by the primary teacher/administrator. SAT/ACT scores are recommended but optional through 2024. Homeschooled students should complete the Texas Foundation High School Program requirements or equivalent. Contact the admissions office for specific documentation requirements for your situation.
Is there a minimum age for undergraduate applicants?

Texas State doesn't have a strict minimum age requirement for undergraduate admission. However, applicants must have completed high school or earned a GED. Students younger than 16 seeking early admission should contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions for special requirements and considerations. All applicants must meet the standard admission requirements regardless of age.
Does Texas State University accept Advanced Placement (AP) credits?

Yes, Texas State accepts AP credits for scores of 3 or higher on most AP exams. Credit hours awarded vary by subject and score. Submit official AP scores through College Board using code 6667. The university also accepts IB, CLEP, and DSST exam credits. Check the university's credit by examination webpage for specific score requirements and credit equivalencies for each exam type.
How can I track my application status after submission?

You can track your application status through your Self-Service Student Center portal at my.txstate.edu. After applying, you'll receive login credentials via email. The portal shows which documents have been received, which are still pending, and your admission decision when available. For additional questions about your application status, contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions directly.
Are recommendation letters required for undergraduate admission?

No, letters of recommendation are not required for general undergraduate admission to Texas State University. However, some specific programs, scholarships, or special circumstances may require letters of recommendation after admission. If you feel letters would strengthen your application, you may submit them, but they are not part of the standard admission review process.
What should I do if I missed the application deadline?

If you missed the deadline, contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions immediately. Late applications may be considered on a case-by-case basis if space is available. You might be able to apply for the next available semester, or in some cases, submit a late application with an explanation letter. Remember that meeting scholarship deadlines is crucial, as late applicants typically aren't considered for merit-based awards.
Does Texas State University offer rolling admissions?

Yes, Texas State uses a rolling admissions process for regular admission. This means applications are reviewed as they are completed, and decisions are sent out continuously rather than on a single date. However, there are still specific priority deadlines (March 1st for Fall) and regular deadlines (May 1st for Fall) to keep in mind. Early Action has a fixed deadline of October 15th with decisions by late November.
Can I apply for admission if I've been out of school for several years?

Yes, Texas State welcomes non-traditional students who have been out of school. You'll need to submit transcripts from high school and any previous college coursework, regardless of when you attended. If accessing old transcripts is difficult, the admissions office can provide guidance. Adult learners may also be interested in the Office of Student Development's resources specifically designed for non-traditional students.
Are there different admission requirements for specific majors?

Yes, some majors have additional admission requirements beyond university standards. Programs in areas like Business, Nursing, Engineering, and Music often have specific prerequisites, higher GPA requirements, or additional application materials. For example, the McCoy College of Business requires a higher GPA, and Fine Arts programs may require auditions or portfolio reviews. Check your intended major's department website for specific requirements.
What is the admissions process for re-admitted students?

Former Texas State students who haven't enrolled for one or more long semesters must apply for readmission. Submit the ApplyTexas application, selecting 'readmission' as your application type. You'll need to provide transcripts from any colleges attended during your absence. Academic standing at the time you left Texas State may affect readmission. Some students may need to appeal or meet with academic advisors before being readmitted.
Are there any requirements for residency to be eligible for in-state tuition?

Yes, to qualify for in-state tuition, you must be a Texas resident for at least 12 months before the semester starts. Requirements include: living in Texas for purposes other than education, financial independence or parental support from a Texas resident, and documentation like Texas driver's license, voter registration, or employment records. Military members, veterans, and their families may qualify for special residency considerations. The university's residency questionnaire determines your status.
How do I apply for admission to graduate programs?

Graduate program applications are processed through The Graduate College. Submit your application through ApplyTexas or GradCAS (depending on program), along with official transcripts from all colleges attended, application fee ($55 domestic/$75 international), and program-specific requirements. Most programs require GRE/GMAT scores, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, and resume. Check your specific program's requirements as they vary by department.
What are the requirements for the transfer application?

Transfer applicants need a minimum 2.0 GPA in all transferable college coursework. Submit official transcripts from every college attended, even if credits don't transfer. With fewer than 30 transferable hours, you must also meet freshman admission requirements and submit high school transcripts. Some programs have higher GPA requirements or prerequisite courses. Use the transfer course equivalency tool on the university website to see how your credits will transfer.
How do I apply for an application deferral?

To defer your admission to a future semester, submit a written request to the Office of Undergraduate Admissions before the start of your original admission term. Deferrals are typically granted for one semester. Include your Texas State ID, reason for deferral, and desired semester in your request. Note that scholarships and financial aid packages don't automatically transfer to deferred terms - you'll need to reapply for these separately.
Can I apply as an undecided major?

Yes, you can apply as an Exploratory Professional (formerly called undecided) major at Texas State. The University College provides academic advising and career exploration resources to help you choose a major. However, you must declare a major before completing 45 credit hours. The PACE program offers structured guidance for exploring different fields of study and career paths while completing core requirements.
How do I verify if my community college credits transfer?

You can verify transferable credits using Texas State's Transfer Course Equivalency System (TES) online. For Texas community colleges, use the Texas Common Course Numbering System (TCCNS) for direct equivalencies. The Transfer Planning Guides show recommended courses by major. For courses not listed, contact the Transfer Credit Office for evaluation. Only courses with grades of C or better from regionally accredited institutions are eligible for transfer.
Is there a specific form for students seeking a double major?

Yes, students pursuing a double major must submit the Second Major Request Form through the academic advising office of their intended second major. This form requires approval signatures from both department chairs. Students should have completed at least one semester at Texas State and be in good academic standing before applying. Each major may have specific GPA requirements and prerequisites. The form must be submitted before the final semester of coursework.
Can I apply if I already have a bachelor's degree?

Yes, you can apply as a post-baccalaureate student if you already have a bachelor's degree. Submit the ApplyTexas application, selecting 'post-baccalaureate' as your application type, along with official transcripts from all previous institutions. Post-baccalaureate students can pursue a second bachelor's degree, teacher certification, or prerequisites for graduate programs. Different admission criteria and tuition rates may apply.
Does Texas State University offer a bridge program for non-traditional students?

Yes, Texas State provides support for non-traditional students through the Office of Student Development. While not a formal bridge program, services include academic coaching, study skills workshops, and peer mentoring. The Student Learning Assistance Center (SLAC) offers additional resources like tutoring and time management workshops. Non-traditional students also have access to specialized orientation programs and academic advising tailored to their needs.
What should I do if my application is denied?

If denied admission, you have several options: 1) Submit an admission appeal with new information or extenuating circumstances not included in your original application, 2) Apply for the PACE program if eligible, 3) Attend a community college and reapply as a transfer student after completing 30 transferable hours, 4) Consider summer admission. Contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions for guidance on the appeals process and alternative pathways to admission.
Are there support services for students applying with disabilities?

Yes, Texas State University offers support services for students with disabilities through the Office of Disability Services. Services include academic accommodations, assistive technology, and disability awareness training for faculty and staff. Students must provide documentation of their disability and meet with a disability specialist to discuss individual needs and accommodations. The university is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to ensure equal access to education for all students.
Can I submit an appeal if I'm denied admission?

Yes, you can appeal a denial decision within 30 days of receiving your notification. Submit an appeal letter to the Office of Undergraduate Admissions explaining any extenuating circumstances or providing new information not included in your original application. Include supporting documentation like updated test scores, new grades, or letters of recommendation. The Admission Appeal Committee typically reviews appeals within 2-3 weeks, and all decisions are final.
Is Texas State University part of the Common Application system?

No, Texas State University does not use the Common Application. All undergraduate applications must be submitted through ApplyTexas (www.applytexas.org), which is the centralized application system for Texas public universities. This includes applications for freshman, transfer, and international students. Create an ApplyTexas account and use Texas State's school code 003615 to begin your application process.
What are the steps for enrolling after I'm accepted?

After acceptance, complete these steps: 1) Accept your admission offer and pay the $150 enrollment deposit, 2) Submit bacterial meningitis vaccination documentation, 3) Complete housing application if planning to live on campus, 4) Register for mandatory New Student Orientation (NSO), 5) Complete online pre-orientation modules, 6) Submit final transcripts, 7) Attend orientation for academic advising and course registration, 8) Set up your Texas State email and NetID.
Are there orientation requirements for new students?

Yes, New Student Orientation (NSO) is mandatory for all incoming freshmen and transfer students. The program includes academic advising, course registration, campus tours, and information sessions about university resources. Students must complete online pre-orientation modules before attending their in-person session. Multiple NSO dates are offered throughout summer for fall enrollment. Spring admits attend orientation in January. Register early as sessions fill quickly.
Can I transfer after one semester at another institution?

Yes, you can apply to transfer after one semester, but you must have completed at least 12 transferable credit hours with a minimum 2.0 GPA. Students with fewer than 30 transferable hours must also meet freshman admission requirements and submit high school transcripts. All transfer credits must be from regionally accredited institutions with grades of C or better. Meet with an admission counselor to discuss your specific situation.
How do I find out about Texas State's diversity programs?

The Office of Student Diversity and Inclusion (SDI) coordinates diversity programs and resources. Programs include the Bobcat Unity Program, multicultural organizations, diversity dialogue series, cultural heritage celebrations, and mentoring initiatives. Visit the SDI office in LBJ Student Center or their website to learn about upcoming events, student organizations, and support services. They also offer diversity training workshops and leadership development opportunities for underrepresented students.
Are there specific application requirements for out-of-state students?

Out-of-state students follow the same basic application process through ApplyTexas. Requirements include: official high school transcripts, optional SAT/ACT scores (through 2024), and a $75 application fee. Out-of-state students pay higher tuition rates unless they qualify for specific scholarships or tuition reduction programs. Some states have reciprocity agreements with Texas. Academic requirements remain the same as for in-state students.
What are the key dates for the admissions process each year?

Key admission dates include: Early Action - October 15th (decision by November); Fall Priority - March 1st (for scholarships); Fall Regular - May 1st; Spring - December 1st; Summer - May 1st. Housing priority deadline is March 1st. FAFSA priority deadline is January 15th. New Student Orientation registration opens in April for fall semester. Check the admissions calendar for specific program deadlines.
How can I contact the Admissions Office for further help?

The Office of Undergraduate Admissions can be reached multiple ways: Phone: 512-245-2364; Email: admissions@txstate.edu; In-person: Richard A. Castro Undergraduate Admissions Center, 429 N. Guadalupe St. Virtual appointments are available through video chat. Office hours are Monday-Friday, 8am-5pm. You can also connect through social media or schedule a campus tour through the admissions website.
What types of financial aid are available at Texas State University?

Texas State offers multiple types of financial aid: 1) Federal grants (Pell, SEOG), 2) State grants (TEXAS Grant, Texas Public Educational Grant), 3) Scholarships (merit-based, departmental, competitive), 4) Federal loans (Direct, PLUS), 5) Work-study programs, 6) The Bobcat Promise program for eligible Texas residents. Submit FAFSA by January 15th priority deadline. Emergency assistance and payment plans are also available through the Financial Aid Office.
How do I apply for financial aid?

To apply for financial aid: 1) Submit FAFSA at fafsa.gov using Texas State school code 003615 by January 15th priority deadline, 2) Create a Texas State student account, 3) Monitor your email for requests for additional documentation, 4) Accept/decline aid offers through the student portal, 5) Complete loan entrance counseling and sign MPN if accepting loans. Texas residents ineligible for FAFSA should complete TASFA instead.
What is the FAFSA, and when should I submit it?

The Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is required to receive federal and state financial aid. Submit it starting October 1st for the following academic year, with Texas State's priority deadline of January 15th. Use school code 003615. The FAFSA determines eligibility for grants, loans, work-study, and some scholarships. Submit it annually to maintain aid. Financial aid workshops and FAFSA completion assistance are available through the Financial Aid Office.
Can I apply for financial aid as an international student?

International students aren't eligible for federal financial aid, but can access other funding options: merit-based scholarships, departmental scholarships, graduate assistantships (for graduate students), and private loans with a U.S. co-signer. The International Student and Scholar Services office provides information about available funding opportunities. F-1 visa students may also be eligible for on-campus employment and Curricular Practical Training (CPT).
What scholarships are available for incoming freshmen?

Incoming freshmen can apply for various scholarships: 1) Academic Achievement Scholarships based on class rank/GPA and test scores, 2) Terry Foundation Scholarships for Texas residents, 3) Departmental scholarships in specific fields, 4) Competitive scholarships like National Merit and Presidential scholarships, 5) Bobcat Promise for eligible Texas residents. Apply by March 1st priority deadline. Complete both admissions and scholarship applications early for best consideration.
What documents are required for a financial aid application?

Required documents include: 1) Completed FAFSA or TASFA with Texas State school code 003615, 2) Tax returns and W-2 forms for student and parents if dependent, 3) Social Security numbers and birth dates for family members, 4) Bank statements and asset information, 5) Records of untaxed income. Additional verification documents may be requested through your student portal. Submit all documents by January 15th priority deadline for fall/spring or March 1st for summer aid.
How is financial aid eligibility determined?

Financial aid eligibility is determined by several factors: 1) Demonstrated financial need based on FAFSA/TASFA results, 2) Enrollment status (minimum half-time: 6 hours undergraduate, 3 hours graduate), 3) Satisfactory Academic Progress (minimum GPA, 67% completion rate, not exceeding maximum attempted hours), 4) U.S. citizenship or eligible non-citizen status, 5) Valid Social Security number, 6) Registration with Selective Service if required, 7) Enrollment in degree-seeking program with courses that count toward your degree.
Are there specific scholarships for Texas residents?

Yes, Texas residents have access to several state-specific aid programs: 1) TEXAS Grant for eligible students with financial need, 2) Texas State Tuition Grant, 3) Texas Public Educational Grant, 4) Bobcat Promise program (covers tuition and fees for eligible students with family incomes under $50,000), 5) Texas College Work Study program. Additional merit-based and departmental scholarships are available. Submit FAFSA/TASFA by January 15th priority deadline and check scholarship portal for specific program deadlines.
What is work-study, and how do I qualify?

Work-study is a financial aid program where students earn money by working part-time at university jobs. To qualify: 1) Submit FAFSA by priority deadline, 2) Demonstrate financial need through FAFSA results, 3) Accept work-study offer in financial aid package, 4) Apply for positions through Jobs4Cats. Students typically work 10-20 hours weekly at minimum wage or higher. Both on-campus and approved off-campus positions are available. Must maintain satisfactory academic progress to keep eligibility.
When will I find out how much financial aid I've been awarded?

After submitting your FAFSA (priority deadline January 15th), you'll receive award notifications through your student portal. The timing depends on when you submit all required documents and complete verification if selected. For fall/spring aid, awards are typically announced by early summer if you met the priority deadline. Monitor your student email for requests for additional documentation, as incomplete files may delay award notifications. You must accept or decline aid offers through the student portal.
Are there grants available at Texas State University?

Yes, Texas State offers several federal and state grants for students with financial need: 1) Federal Pell Grant, 2) Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant (SEOG), 3) TEACH Grant, 4) Iraq-Afghanistan Service Grant, 5) TEXAS Grant, 6) Texas State Tuition Grant, 7) Texas Public Educational Grant. Grants are gift aid that doesn't need to be repaid. Submit FAFSA by January 15th priority deadline to be considered. Award amounts vary based on financial need and program requirements.
Can I receive both a scholarship and a grant?

Yes, you can receive both scholarships and grants simultaneously. Many students combine multiple forms of aid including: 1) Merit-based scholarships, 2) Need-based grants like Pell Grant and TEXAS Grant, 3) Departmental scholarships, 4) Outside scholarships. There's no limit to scholarship amounts, but total aid cannot exceed your cost of attendance. The Financial Aid Office will help coordinate your aid package to maximize your benefits while staying within federal and state guidelines.
How can I estimate my financial aid package?

To estimate your financial aid: 1) Use the Net Price Calculator on Texas State's website to get a preliminary estimate, 2) Submit FAFSA early to receive your official Expected Family Contribution (EFC), 3) Review your Student Aid Report (SAR) after FAFSA submission, 4) Check scholarship eligibility based on your academic profile, 5) Contact Financial Aid Office for personalized estimates. Final packages are typically announced by early summer if you meet the January 15th priority deadline.
Do I need to reapply for financial aid every year?

Yes, you must reapply for financial aid each academic year by submitting a new FAFSA or TASFA by the January 15th priority deadline. This annual renewal is required to: 1) Maintain eligibility for federal/state grants, 2) Continue work-study participation, 3) Receive need-based scholarships, 4) Keep Bobcat Promise benefits. Your aid package may change yearly based on updated financial information, academic performance, and maintaining satisfactory academic progress requirements.
How do I check the status of my financial aid application?

You can check your financial aid application status through several methods: 1) Log into your Texas State student portal and check the Financial Aid tab, 2) Monitor your Texas State email for notifications and requests for additional documentation, 3) Contact the Financial Aid Office directly at 512-245-2315 or financialaid@txstate.edu. Remember to check regularly as additional documentation may be requested. Your aid won't be processed until all required documents are received.
Are there loans available for undergraduate students?

Yes, undergraduate students have access to several loan options: 1) Federal Direct Subsidized Loans (need-based, government pays interest while in school), 2) Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans (available regardless of need), 3) Parent PLUS loans (taken by parents for dependent students), 4) Private loans through banks or credit unions. To apply for federal loans, submit FAFSA by January 15th priority deadline. All federal loans require entrance counseling and signing a Master Promissory Note (MPN).
Can I get financial aid if I'm only attending part-time?

Yes, part-time students can receive financial aid if enrolled in at least 6 credit hours per semester for undergraduates or 3 hours for graduates. However, aid amounts are typically reduced proportionally to enrollment status. Pell Grants, student loans, and some state grants are available for part-time students. Some scholarships may require full-time enrollment, so check specific requirements. Submit FAFSA by the priority deadline regardless of enrollment status.
What happens if my financial aid doesn't cover all costs?

If financial aid doesn't cover all costs, you have several options: 1) Set up an installment payment plan to spread remaining costs over the semester, 2) Apply for additional private loans with a co-signer, 3) Consider Parent PLUS loans if you're a dependent student, 4) Apply for departmental or external scholarships, 5) Check eligibility for work-study or student employment. The Student Business Services office can help evaluate payment options and set up payment plans before payment deadlines.
Does Texas State University offer emergency financial aid?

Yes, Texas State offers emergency assistance through several programs: 1) Emergency grant funding for unexpected financial hardships, 2) Bobcat Cares emergency grants for COVID-19 related expenses, 3) Short-term emergency loans for immediate educational expenses, 4) Emergency housing and food assistance through Student Emergency Services, 5) Technology assistance for academic needs. Contact the Financial Aid Office or Student Emergency Services to apply for emergency aid.
How are scholarships awarded?

Scholarships are awarded based on various criteria: 1) Academic merit (GPA, test scores, class rank), 2) Financial need from FAFSA/TASFA results, 3) Specific major or department requirements, 4) Special talents or achievements, 5) First-generation student status. Most university scholarships require the general scholarship application through the scholarship portal by March 1st priority deadline. Departmental scholarships may have separate applications and deadlines. Competitive scholarships often require essays, recommendations, or interviews.
Can I lose my financial aid if my grades drop?

Yes, you must maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) to keep financial aid: 1) Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 for undergraduates, 3.0 for graduates, 2) Complete 67% of all attempted credit hours, 3) Not exceed 150% of your degree program's required hours. If you fail to meet SAP requirements, you'll be placed on financial aid warning. You may appeal if extenuating circumstances affected your academic performance. The Financial Aid Office offers SAP workshops and academic planning assistance.
How can I qualify for a merit-based scholarship?

To qualify for merit-based scholarships: 1) Meet minimum GPA requirements (typically 3.0+), 2) Submit test scores if available (can strengthen application), 3) Apply by March 1st priority deadline, 4) Complete the general scholarship application through the scholarship portal, 5) Maintain strong academic performance. Additional requirements may include leadership experience, extracurricular activities, or specific major enrollment. Competitive scholarships may require essays or interviews. Check departmental scholarships for major-specific opportunities.
What is the difference between a subsidized and an unsubsidized loan?

The main differences are: Subsidized loans are need-based with government paying interest while you're in school, during grace period, and deferment. Unsubsidized loans are available regardless of financial need, but interest accrues from disbursement date. Both require at least half-time enrollment and FAFSA completion. Subsidized loans have lower borrowing limits and are only for undergraduates, while unsubsidized loans are available to both undergraduate and graduate students with higher limits.
Are there scholarships for specific majors?

Yes, Texas State offers departmental scholarships for specific majors and fields of study. Each academic department manages their own scholarship programs with unique eligibility requirements and deadlines. Contact your department's main office or check their website for available opportunities. Additionally, the College of Science and Engineering, McCoy College of Business, and College of Fine Arts and Communication offer college-level scholarships. Apply through the general scholarship application portal and check departmental websites for any supplemental applications.
Can I apply for multiple scholarships?

Yes, you are encouraged to apply for multiple scholarships to maximize your funding opportunities. The general scholarship application automatically considers you for all university-wide scholarships you qualify for. You can also apply for: 1) Departmental scholarships, 2) College-specific awards, 3) Competitive scholarships, 4) External/private scholarships. There's no limit to the number of scholarships you can receive, but total aid cannot exceed your cost of attendance. Submit all applications by respective deadlines and monitor your email for additional requirements.
How do I appeal a financial aid decision?

To appeal a financial aid decision: 1) Submit a written appeal letter explaining special circumstances affecting your financial situation, 2) Provide supporting documentation (medical bills, proof of job loss, etc.), 3) Complete the Special Circumstances Appeal Form from the Financial Aid Office, 4) Submit all materials to the Financial Aid Office for review. Appeals are reviewed case-by-case and typically take 2-3 weeks. Common appeal reasons include: loss of income, medical expenses, or other significant changes in financial circumstances not reflected on FAFSA.
Can graduate students apply for financial aid?

Yes, graduate students can apply for financial aid by submitting the FAFSA with Texas State's school code (003615). Graduate students are eligible for: 1) Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans, 2) Graduate PLUS loans, 3) Work-study opportunities, 4) Departmental scholarships and fellowships, 5) Graduate assistantships. Full-time status requires 6 credit hours for master's students and 5 hours for doctoral students. The March 15th FAFSA priority deadline applies to graduate students.
What is satisfactory academic progress (SAP) for financial aid?

Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) requirements for financial aid include: 1) Maintaining minimum cumulative Texas State GPA (2.0 undergraduate, 3.0 graduate), 2) Completing at least 67% of all attempted coursework, 3) Not exceeding maximum attempted hours toward degree (150% of program length). Students who don't meet SAP standards are placed on financial aid warning. Additional program-specific requirements may apply. SAP status is reviewed each semester and affects eligibility for all types of financial aid.
How can I increase my financial aid package?

Are there financial aid options for students with disabilities?

The Office of Disability Services can help coordinate with Financial Aid to ensure appropriate accommodations and support.
Can I use financial aid for summer courses?

Yes, you can use financial aid for summer courses if you: 1) Have remaining aid eligibility from the academic year, 2) Enroll in at least 6 credit hours for undergraduate or 3 hours for graduate students, 3) Submit a Summer Aid Application through your student portal, 4) Meet Satisfactory Academic Progress requirements. The priority deadline for summer aid is March 1st. Available summer aid includes Pell Grants, student loans, and work-study. Note that using aid in summer may affect your fall/spring aid amounts.
What is the Texas Public Educational Grant?

The Texas Public Educational Grant (TPEG) is a need-based state grant program that provides aid to eligible Texas residents, non-residents, and international students. Eligibility requirements include: 1) Demonstrated financial need through FAFSA/TASFA, 2) Enrollment in at least 6 credit hours, 3) Maintaining satisfactory academic progress. Award amounts vary based on need and available funding. The grant does not need to be repaid. Priority consideration is given to students who submit FAFSA/TASFA by the January 15th deadline.
How does the university calculate cost of attendance?

The university calculates cost of attendance (COA) by combining: 1) Direct costs: tuition, fees, on-campus housing and meal plans, 2) Indirect costs: books, supplies, transportation, personal expenses, off-campus housing allowance. COA varies based on residency status, housing choice, and enrollment level. The Financial Aid Office reviews and updates COA annually to reflect current expenses. This total represents the maximum financial aid you can receive from all sources combined.
Can I get financial aid for study abroad programs?

How does parent income affect financial aid?

Parent income directly impacts need-based financial aid for dependent students through the FAFSA's Expected Family Contribution (EFC) calculation. Factors considered include: 1) Parents' taxed/untaxed income, 2) Assets and investments, 3) Household size, 4) Number of family members in college. Higher parent income generally means higher EFC and less need-based aid eligibility. However, merit-based scholarships and unsubsidized loans are available regardless of parent income. Independent students are evaluated based on their own income.
Are there scholarships for transfer students?

Awards are based on academic achievement, leadership, and other criteria specified by donors.
Can I defer my student loans after graduation?

Yes, federal student loans typically offer several deferment options after graduation: 1) Automatic 6-month grace period after graduation, 2) Economic hardship deferment, 3) Graduate school enrollment deferment, 4) Military service deferment, 5) Unemployment deferment. Interest may still accrue during deferment periods on unsubsidized loans. Contact your loan servicer to discuss specific deferment options and requirements. Alternative repayment plans like income-based repayment are also available.
What happens to my financial aid if I withdraw from classes?

If you withdraw from classes, several things happen: 1) If withdrawal is before the 60% point of the semester, you must repay unearned portions of federal Title IV aid, 2) Unofficial withdrawals (all U's, W's, or I's) require federal withdrawal calculations, 3) Your future aid eligibility may be affected if you don't meet Satisfactory Academic Progress requirements, 4) You must complete an Official Withdrawal Request form and speak with Financial Aid before withdrawing. Contact Financial Aid for a personalized review of how withdrawal will affect your specific aid package.
Are there grants specifically for minority students?

How do I apply for the Bobcat Promise program?

No separate application is needed - eligible students are automatically considered when FAFSA/TASFA is submitted. The program covers tuition and mandatory fees for up to 4 years.

Are there any restrictions on using financial aid for off-campus housing?

Aid disbursement first covers direct costs (tuition and fees), then remaining funds are released to you for indirect costs like off-campus housing. The amount available for housing depends on your total aid package and cannot exceed the housing allowance in your COA.
How do I maintain my scholarship eligibility?
